content_html:
A junk drawer becomes chaotic because it receives objects with no better home, not because it lacks enough dividers. A system that lasts starts by removing trash and duplicates and limiting the drawer to a small set of everyday items.

Empty the drawer and remove what no longer belongs

Discard wrappers, dried pens, and parts with no known use; send batteries, medicines, and other special waste to the proper disposal route. Do not buy organizers until you know what actually deserves to go back.

Create a few categories that make sense together

Writing tools, small tools, tape, spare keys, or charging accessories can each have a compartment. If one category takes up half the drawer, it probably deserves a dedicated home elsewhere.

Measure the drawer before choosing dividers

Width, depth, and usable height determine what trays fit without blocking the drawer. Combine small bins or adjustable dividers and leave one space for longer items that genuinely belong there.

Leave a small buffer for new items

If every compartment starts completely full, the next new object creates another pile. Leave a little buffer and spend a few minutes every few months returning misplaced items to their permanent homes.
